free_tier.stated: 100 GB total storage on the free Community plan, but with a 3 GB limit per dataset or project. And their own docs are stricter still: 'Dataset ingested to data.world: 1 GB'; 'Size of a file in a dataset: 1 GB'; 'Number of files in a dataset: 250'; 'Project: 1 GB'. The 100 GB aggregate is therefore unreachable in practice because each unit can only be 1 GB.

egress.terms: Free but rate-shaped: 'Number of burst streams API calls: 5 in the first second … then 1 per second'; streamed records capped at 1 MiB; streamed request 1 GB.

record.tooling: A real developer API (developer.data.world) plus SQL over datasets, so it is programmatically clean. The API surface is the best part of the product and the quota is the worst.
record.chaining: 20 private projects/datasets × 3 GB, or the 100 GB aggregate if per-unit limits were the only constraint. In practice 1 GB per dataset × 100 units is the ceiling, so sharding to 500 GB means 500 units. Three times the published unit count.
record.limits_note: fails-quota by ~500x for the requirement, and the platform is mid-acquisition ('ServiceNow to acquire data.world'), which is a reliability signal. Free tier is aimed at public data projects, not private bulk storage.
record.reliability_note: Ownership change in progress (ServiceNow). The docs' 1 GB ingest limit contradicts the marketing 3 GB figure. Believe the docs.

opened: '20 private projects/datasets', '20 live tables', '3GB limit per dataset or project', '100GB total storage size'; and the banner 'ServiceNow to acquire data.world'.
same page: the free tier is framed around 'Open Data' access, i.e. read-side value, not storage.

record.price_per_tb_month: Community free (100 GB aggregate, 1-3 GB per unit). Professional Community plan $12/month for 20 private projects — ~$120/TB/month against a 100 GB pool, though the per-unit 1 GB cap makes the pool theoretical.
